runs.v: is a cover fitted over or inside a gutter trough that blocks leaves, pine needles, seed pods, and shingle grit while letting water pass into the gutter. A gutter guard reduces clogging and overflow rather than eliminating gutter cleaning.

Gutters direct rainwater away from homes to prevent water damage, foundation erosion, and basement flooding, and proper gutters protect homes from mold growth, mildew, and damaged siding. Guards protect a house by preventing clogs from leaves and debris, keeping the gutter system flowing to the downspouts, not onto windows and landscaping; clogged gutters lead to water backup at roofs and foundations on residential and commercial buildings alike. faqs.q: What gutter guard works best under Montclair's tree canopy?

runs.v: Micro-mesh, the finest-filtration type. Which company offers the best gutter guards? Many installers specialize in one brand, but the best guard depends on the trees overhead and a correct fit.

faqs.q: Do gutter guards eliminate gutter cleaning in Montclair?

runs.v: No. In a 2025 This Old House survey of 1,000 homeowners, about 30% stopped cleaning while 63% still cleaned yearly, so plan to maintain the guard.

faqs.q: Should the gutter be repaired before guards are installed in Montclair?

runs.v: Yes. A guard over a sagging or leaking gutter locks in the defect, so the run is fixed first.

faqs.q: Do gutter guards prevent ice dams on Montclair homes?

runs.v: No. Guards can ease ice packing in a leaf-filled trough, and freeze-thaw cycles worsen eave ice in clogged gutters, but the root cause is attic heat loss, per University of Minnesota Extension, and an ice barrier protects the eave, per 2021 IRC Section R905.1.2.

faqs.q: How long do gutter guards last on a Montclair home?

runs.v: Micro-mesh lasts longest of the five types, often with a 20 to 25-year or lifetime manufacturer warranty, while foam and brush guards last a few years, per EcoWatch.
